findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an earlier-adopted repo resumes an isolated check-removal fix whose previous review recorded a spotted item.
The filter excludes `plans/spotted/` but still counts the legacy `plans/spotted.json` as another change. Earlier Forge releases wrote that file, and `src/forge/spotted.py:85` still reads it as a Forge record. After upgrading, close therefore refuses an otherwise isolated removal whose earlier review changed that list, preventing it from reaching the shared-check wait.
findings.title: Functional: Exclude Forge’s spotted records from the isolation check

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a retained check has not reported, or a mixed fix has unpushed commits on an existing pull request.
Every removal-only case supplies `forge-pr-check`. The queued cases would still pass if the shared required list were empty, because `src/forge/checks.py:289` also waits for queued checks that are not named. Separately, the product and conflict cases push the mixed HEAD before close at lines 77–80, so the remote-SHA assertion at line 103 cannot detect close pushing that same HEAD before refusing. Exercise a missing retained check and leave the existing PR's remote head behind the mixed commit.
